result:
All 1330 tests pass. Summary of the change (matching upstream PR #1328):

- **`src/attr/_make.py`** — `Converter.__init__` now builds a `self.__call__` adapter closure based on `takes_self`/`takes_field`, so a `Converter` instance can always be invoked uniformly as `converter(value, instance, field)` and it dispatches to the wrapped callable with the right subset of arguments.
- **`pipe_converter`** (inside `pipe()`) was buggy — it built a dict keyed by `(takes_self, takes_field)` whose values were the *boolean flags themselves*, so it accidentally passed `True`/`False` as positional arguments instead of the actual `inst`/`field` values. Replaced with `c(val, inst, field) if isinstance(c, Converter) else c(val)`, relying on the new adapter.
- **`tests/test_make.py`** — added a parametrized test exercising all four `takes_self`/`takes_field` combinations to verify the adapter passes exactly the right arguments through.
- **`changelog.d/1328.change.md`** — added a news fragment.

Verified with the full test suite (1330 passed) run against the local `src` (note: a globally installed `attrs` package shadows it unless `PYTHONPATH=src` is set — worth knowing if you run tests directly).
